extraction.Name: William Walker
extraction.Refused/Protested: There was no protest made by Walker
extraction.Recorded patent: Walker never had recorded, (look up record in Brule Co)
extraction.Occupation/Income: William Walker was Indian police at time
extraction.NOTES: Patent was delivered to Walker by Major McGlaughin; patent was receipted for / not receipted for (unclear from document); Walker received letter from Sup't Marble through Mr O'Shea farmer of the Big Bend district to take one Mrs Arrow to Agency, letter dated Apr 23rd 1918; when he arrived Major McGlaughin called William Walker into the office and told him he was one of the Indians that was going to be turned loose; a year afterwards he received a letter from Sup't Marble to come to the agency that he had a patent in fee and to come shoot the arrow before the inspector; he arrived too late to shoot the arrow; they gave him the arrow to keep; McGlaughin gave him a citizen paper and also the patent.
